entry.title: Combined summary - BIP 119 CTV activation client
entry.summary: Following a unanimous agreement on activation parameters, the deployment of CTV (BIP-119) has been enhanced with several critical updates to improve accessibility and comprehension for users and developers. A direct link to the activation client's repository has been included on the project's website to ensure easy access to essential tools and information. This addition aims to facilitate smoother transitions and implementations by providing resources readily available at [GitHub](https://github.com/ctv-activation/activation-client). The deployment details have been clearly outlined, with significant milestones and technical specifications set for the implementation phase. The activation is scheduled to commence on March 30, 2026, and conclude by March 30, 2027. A key milestone includes achieving a minimum activation height of 1001952 by May 2027. A consensus mechanism requiring a 90% threshold over a span of 2016 blocks has been established, creating a robust framework for achieving broad support within the community. Additionally, an archive link has been made available at [archive.is](https://archive.is/o6QgT), providing stakeholders with access to snapshots of the project’s progress and documentation. This archive serves as a valuable reference point for historical data and decision-making processes related to the CTV deployment. These developments not only mark significant progress in deploying CTV (BIP-119) but also offer comprehensive guidance and information to all parties involved, ensuring that the project achieves successful implementation and widespread adoption within the specified timeframe. Despite these advancements, there remains skepticism within the broader Bitcoin community concerning the upcoming activation of CTV. To address this, it is suggested that demonstrating practical software use cases, particularly how CTV can aid in high fee environments, would be beneficial. Such demonstrations could allow average users to test functionalities on their own devices, potentially increasing acceptance and support for CTV. However, the development of such demonstrative software is acknowledged as significantly delayed, indicating a need for accelerated effort in this area to align with community expectations and enhance the project's viability.
